subject: Decision gate synthesis: token levers, batching, and budget asks
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Tom Zhao <tom.zhao@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Jul 9, 2026 at 4:32 PM -0700
Subject: Decision gate synthesis: token levers, batching, and budget asks

Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps. I’ve kept this focused on the economics and the concrete levers we discussed.

Key pain points you described
- High and variable token spend on conversational flows (billing spikes when support chat surges).
- Repeated priming (system + instructions) across requests — we estimated ~25–30% of tokens are repeatable.
- Tight latency SLOs for UI chat (99th percentile target ~500ms) plus a hard budget gate next quarter.
- Procurement & security constraints: prefer PO-based pilot spend, need SOC2 evidence.

Goals we agreed
- Reduce unit cost (per effective response) while keeping 99p latency within 500ms for core chat paths.
- Prove predictable economics in a 4–6 week pilot with measurable per-message savings.
- Deliver a recommended rollout plan for production after pilot (model choice, batching/cache config, autoscale policy).

Quantitative baseline & leverage assumptions (ballpark from today’s discussion)
- Current baseline: ~120M tokens / month across chat + admin prompts (~$18k/mo at current rate).
- Expected lever impact (pilot targets):
  • KV/prefix caching of templates & prompts => ~15–25% token reduction on repeated flows.
  • Batching where latency allows (async/bulk workflows) => up to 20% token and compute efficiency on those paths.
  • Model variant + int8 quantization on non-latency-critical routes => additional ~10–20% CPU/GPU spend reduction.
- Conservative combined pilot estimate: ~25–30% net reduction on scoped traffic (pilot slice), equating to ~$4.5–$6k/month savings if sustained.

Integration effort & timeline
- Estimate: 2 sprints (4 weeks) engineering + 1 week SRE/ops enablement to lock observability and alerts.
- Pilot window: 4 weeks post-integration for metrics collection and final recommendation.

Open constraints you flagged
- Procurement: pilot ceiling preferred ~$25k (PO) rather than open usage billing.
- Security: SOC2 attestation required for any non-demo environment.
- Latency: must maintain 99p ~500ms for the UI chat path; can route lower-priority traffic to lower-cost variants.

Next steps (proposed — I’ll own the coordination)
1) Send mutual action plan & pilot cost model (attached).
2) Match pilot scope to the $25k PO threshold; we’ll produce a cost-capped pilot option.
3) Schedule procurement call with Aisha to confirm PO/contract terms (cc’d if you approve).
4) Technical kickoff with engineering + SRE in week of Aug 3.

Attachments: Ledgerly_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx, Pilot_Cost_Model_v1.xlsx, SOC2_attestation_summary.pdf

If this captures today’s memo, reply “confirm” and we’ll send an updated MAP that fits the $25k ceiling.

—
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Tom Zhao <tom.zhao@ledgerly.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@ledgerly.com>
Date: Thu, Jul 9, 2026 at 5:07 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Decision gate synthesis: token levers, batching, and budget asks

Aditya — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few items from our side:

• Budget constraint: Procurement will only approve a PO up to $25k for a pilot this quarter. Any pilot that expects overruns will need pre-approval.
• Security: SOC2 Type II proof will be required before we move beyond sandbox. Aisha is copying procurement.
• Latency fallback: we need an explicit fallback / circuit-breaker if batching causes UI regressions — route to a smaller model or disable batching for the UI path.

We like the idea of a scoped pilot focused on the high-volume repeated prompts — that’s where we see the biggest token upside.

If you can send an updated MAP that locks to $25k and includes the latency fallback and SOC2 references, I’ll share that with Aisha and schedule a short PO alignment call next week.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Zhao
Head of Product, Ledgerly
tom.zhao@ledgerly.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 8:15 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Decision gate synthesis: token levers, batching, and budget asks

Quick internal note — agree with Tom’s asks. Suggest the following tactical changes to fit the $25k PO:

1) Pilot scope: limit to two high-volume flows (support chat + account-summary generation).
2) Integration: one engineer + one SRE for 4 weeks (we absorb one week of on-call during ramp).
3) Safety rails: token cap alerts, automated fallback to low-cost model if 99p latency > 500ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows.
4) Credit: offer up to $3k in usage credits for the pilot to reduce procurement friction (presented as a promotional offset).

I’ll draft the MAP language to make the PO straightforward. Ben — can you prepare a slimmed-down cost worksheet reflecting the $25k max and the expected 25% conservative savings on the scoped traffic?

—Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Tom Zhao <tom.zhao@ledgerly.com>, Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 10:12 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Decision gate synthesis: token levers, batching, and budget asks — MAP & pilot option (budget-capped)

Tom / Aisha — appreciate the quick response and the procurement constraints. Attached is a tightened Mutual Action Plan and a slim pilot cost worksheet. Highlights below so you have the numbers up front: 

Pilot option (budget-capped: $25k PO) — scope & economics- Scope: 2 flows (support chat templated replies + account-summary reports).- Integration: 4 weeks (1 eng, 1 SRE).- Pilot window: 4 weeks of measurement after integration.- Safety rails: token cap, 99p latency alerting and automated model fallback.

Costs & ROI (conservative case)- One-time integration & ops: $18k (engineering + SRE enablement).- Variable usage & margins (capped): $7k (estimated usage for pilot slice).- Total pilot cost: $25k (fits procurement PO ceiling).

Conservative benefit (run-rate if results sustained across production)- Expected token/compute reduction on scoped traffic: 25% => ~$4.5k/month saved at current baseline for the scoped traffic.- If we expand beyond the pilot to 50% of traffic with similar efficiency, expected monthly savings would be ~$9–10k, giving payback on the $25k integration in ~3 months (conservative assumptions).

Commitments from Redwood- SOC2 attestation document included (SOC2_attestation_summary.pdf).- We’ll implement the latency fallback and publish the exact triggering thresholds in the MAP.- Up to $3k promotional usage credit to reduce procurement friction (applied to pilot usage line, not the integration fee).

Immediate asks from Ledgerly
1) Approve this MAP with PO path (we’ll prepare an invoice/statement of work tied to the PO).
2) Quick procurement call: Aisha — can you do 30 minutes on Mon Jul 13 or Tue Jul 14 to confirm PO terms?
3) Technical kickoff: propose Aug 3 for a joint 60-minute session (eng + SRE).

I’ll update the HubSpot deal and upload the MAP to the shared drive after your confirmation (links below).

HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/LDG-2026-137
Drive MAP: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPilotFolder

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.
